title: Bridgeway Systems - Compatibility Playbook & Cost Migration Demo
next_steps: Alex to send tailored pricing and cost comparison spreadsheet by 2026-11-10
Priya to share Redwood Console quickstart guide and Optimize recommendations link
Schedule 2-week pilot to run Bridgeway chat workload on Redwood Dedicated (proposed start 2026-11-20)
Security to run a brief SOC2/KMS Q&A with Omar on 2026-11-12
action_items: Alex Kim: Send tailored pricing / TPS-cost model (due 2026-11-10)
Priya Singh: Share Console screenshots, batching & quantization playbook (due 2026-11-09)
Marco Alvarez: Prep pilot runbook and sample benchmark script (due 2026-11-17)

summary: Introductory migration demo focused on API compatibility, cost/latency tradeoffs, and pilot plan. Bridgeway is evaluating replacing current OpenAI/Together endpoints with Redwood API for lower inference cost and better VPC deployment options. Security and compliance are blockers; agreed to pilot and follow up with SOC2/KMS details.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
Security: KMS, SSO, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Chris Moreno (Bridgeway): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Alex. We got a handful of folks here from platform and security.
[00:11] Dana Li (Platform Eng): Hi all. Dana here.
[00:13] Priya Singh (SE): Morning, team. I'm Priya from Redwood, I'll drive the demo and the compatibility mapping.
[00:18] Alex Kim: Quick agenda: 1) high level parity map from your current providers to Redwood API, 2) Console and Optimize walkthrough, 3) security & deployment options, 4) pilot next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:29] Juliette Moreau (Product): Yes, that sounds good. We're especially keen on the cost model and how function / tool calls map over.
[00:35] [00:36] Priya Singh: Great. To orient — Redwood exposes a simple REST/SDK surface for text gen, chat, embeddings. We try to mirror the common patterns from OpenAI and Anthropic so minimal code changes. For Together-specific features, we usually map to the Redwood streaming + function call patterns.
[00:50] Marco Alvarez (SE): I'll jump in on the technical mapping. Example: your current endpoint that uses openai.ChatCompletion calls with messages -> map to redwood.chat.create with nearly identical message envelope. There are some subtle differences in parameter names, and we surface model variants in the model catalog. We also expose per-request routing hints (like prefer-dedicated) which are useful in a hybrid setup.
[01:12] Dana Li: OK, curious about KV cache behavior — we rely heavily on session caching for long chats to save latency. How does Redwood handle that vs the way we did it on Together?
[01:21] Priya Singh: Good question. Redwood maintains a KV cache for the past key/values and allows prefix caching across requests. For your use-case we recommend enabling prefix caching + upsert-style keys when you have stable session ids. It behaves similarly to Together but we expose controls in Console to tune TTL and eviction and we also support client-side pinned KV if you need absolute control.
[01:42] Omar Patel (Security): Real quick on encryption: we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs. Do you support bringing our key and full request audit trails?
[01:51] Marco Alvarez: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS integration and HSM options. Audit logs with token-level traces are available in Console; for Dedicated we can push more detailed logs to your SIEM. I should note that hosted API can also integrate with customer KMS for at-rest encryption in some regions; we'll follow up with specifics.
[02:12] Alex Kim: I'll add that in the security Q&A. Omar, we can do a short SOC2/KMS session next week — I put that as an action item.
[02:21] [02:23] Priya Singh: Switching to a quick live demo — I'll share my screen. (screen share noise) Okay, you'll see Console > Models > Bridgeway-sample. On the left is the model catalog; you can see verified throughput numbers next to each variant.
[02:38] Juliette Moreau: The throughput numbers — are those comparable to what we saw on OpenAI in our internal benchmarks?
[02:43] Priya Singh: The numbers are measured on our standard sequences; that said we can run your exact sample workload during the pilot to get apples-to-apples. Console's Optimize tab will recommend batching and quant profiles given the sample histogram you upload.
[02:58] [03:00] Marco Alvarez: One practical note: token accounting is slightly different depending on whether you use streaming or non-streaming responses. Redwood charges per output token similarly to OpenAI, but Optimize shows you effective cost per 1k output tokens after batching/caching savings, which is usually where the delta shows up.
[03:18] Dana Li: Can you show an example of a function / tool call mapping? We do a lot of retrieval augmented generation where the model returns structured tool outputs.
[03:26] Priya Singh: Sure. (typing) Example: Together had a 'tool_results' callback with a nested payload. On Redwood we map that into the functions API — you define the function schema in the request and Redwood returns a structured function_call with the JSON payload. We also support streaming partial function outputs so your app can start processing sooner.
[03:45] Chris Moreno: That streaming partial tool output is big for us — reduces latency spikes.
[03:49] Priya Singh: Yup. And you can set a 'partial_threshold' so you get a chunk when X bytes are ready.
[03:56] [04:00] Alex Kim: Let's talk about Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private briefly — you mentioned Bridgeway has some regulated workloads?
[04:07] Chris Moreno: Yes, certain healthcare-adjacent partners require data residency and dedicated tenancy. We wanted to understand tradeoffs and effort to move on-prem or VPC.
[04:17] Marco Alvarez: Hosted (the simplest) gives fastest ramp; Dedicated gets you reserved GPU pools and predictable SLOs; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives the strictest control: private control plane and we can hand off an air-gapped bundle if needed. For compliance, Private lets you integrate with your KMS and restrict egress.
[04:36] Omar Patel: Time to first byte and latency SLO are important. On Dedicated, what latencies do you guarantee for 1-to-1 small chat calls?
[04:46] Priya Singh: Our Dedicated performance SLA depends on the commit level, but typical 95th-percentile latency for short sequences is in the 60-120ms range for many models. For your low-latency use-case we can prioritize models compiled/optimized for NVLink clusters; we'll propose a benchmark plan in the pilot.
[05:05] [05:08] Juliette Moreau: Cost-wise we saw some preliminary numbers — are there any gotchas when porting prompts that could increase token usage?
[05:15] Marco Alvarez: Yes, prompt engineering differences can cause token shifts: role naming, metadata blocks, or redundant system messages. Our migration playbook recommends a two-step approach: 1) code-level parity pass (ensure message envelope maps cleanly), 2) token audit run via Console with sample traces to estimate delta. Optimize then recommends batching and quantization to offset.
[05:36] Dana Li: About quantization — is that automatic or do we need to recompile models?
[05:41] Priya Singh: For Dedicated we support pre-compiled quantized variants. Optimize will suggest a quant profile (e.g., 4-bit Q4 or mixed) given your quality thresholds. We run internal A/B to validate hallucination/regression risk; you'll get a quality delta estimate per prompt set.
[06:00] [06:05] Chris Moreno: Can Redwood replicate the system-prompt style we use to control persona? We had issues on Anthropic where the prompt framing changed outputs.
[06:13] Priya Singh: Yes — Redwood's chat API accepts the same 'system' role. We also support structured restarts and 'pinned system blocks' that persist across a session so you don't have to resend the entire system prompt each time, which saves tokens.
[06:30] Alex Kim: I'm going to surface a customer example — Quanta Systems migrated similarly and reduced cost per conversation by ~35% after enabling prefix caching and our Optimize recommendations. Marco, do you want to show the sample benchmark spreadsheet?
[06:43] Marco Alvarez: Sure. (switching tabs) Here's the comparison table: baseline (OpenAI/Together) vs Redwood Hosted vs Redwood Dedicated. Note columns for median latency, 95p latency, effective cost per 1k tokens, and incident rate. The pilot will fill the 'Bridgeway sample' column so we can be precise.
[07:02] [07:05] Juliette Moreau: We'd like to see that filled with our chat traces. Where do we upload those securely?
[07:12] Priya Singh: You can upload sample traces directly into Console's Optimize workspace; files are encrypted at rest and we can set an access expiration. Alternatively, we can accept a secure S3 snapshot if that's preferable.
[07:24] Omar Patel: Security question — retention policy. We cannot allow long-term storage in some cases.
[07:29] Marco Alvarez: Console allows you to set retention windows per workspace. For Dedicated or Private we do not store customer payloads beyond configured retention; we'll include the retention settings in the pilot runbook.
[07:45] [07:48] Chris Moreno: Ok, high level makes sense. One more thing — feature parity: are there any behavioral differences around hallucination mitigation features (e.g., safety layers) compared to Anthropic?
[07:58] Priya Singh: Redwood supports probabilistic and rule-based safety layers. Model-side safety depends on the underlying model; our Optimize tooling can detect regressions with eval prompt sets. We also offer reranking and response-filter hooks as an extra layer.
[08:16] Alex Kim: Let's talk timeline and pilot shape. We're proposing a 2-week pilot to run a couple of your most common chat patterns against a dedicated pool with our caching + batching enabled. Marco, what do you need from Bridgeway to get started?
08:30] Marco Alvarez: We'll need: 1) sample prompt traces (anonymized), 2) expected QPS and concurrency targets, 3) a short list of critical prompts for quality thresholding, and 4) security constraints (KMS/SAML/retention). With that we can provision a pilot environment and run apples-to-apples benchmarks.
[08:52] Juliette Moreau: On the tie-ins to product, we want to validate response fidelity — can we do a blind A/B between current provider and Redwood?
[08:59] Priya Singh: Absolutely. We'll set up a double-blind A/B runner in the pilot and return quality metrics and flags for hallucination/regression.
[09:10] [09:12] Omar Patel: One last ask — compliance questionnaire. We'll need a completed security questionnaire for procurement.
[09:17] Alex Kim: We'll attach the standard security pack and SOC2 docs in the follow-up. Action items noted.
[09:24] Priya Singh: Quick demo wrap-up: Console > Optimize shows a recommended batch size here; toggling batching from 1 to 8 shows a non-linear cost drop. Also the model catalog highlights quantized variants with an estimated quality delta.
[09:40] Dana Li: On SDK changes, will we need to change error handling? We currently rely on a retry-on-429 pattern.
[09:47] Marco Alvarez: Redwood surface returns a 429 for rate limits as well, and we expose headers with retry-after and queue position for Dedicated bursts. We also support streaming reconnect semantics to avoid token duplication.
[09:59] [10:00] Juliette Moreau: Great. Can you recap next steps?
[10:03] Alex Kim: Sure — recap: Alex will send pricing and cost model, Priya will share Console and Optimize docs, Marco will prepare pilot runbook and benchmark script, Omar will send list of security requirements and questionnaire answers. We aim to start pilot around 2026-11-20. Any blockers?
[10:20] Chris Moreno: None immediate. Omar will review the security docs but we expect a short loop.
[10:24] Dana Li: One small thing — do you have a terraform provider or IaC we can use for Dedicated infra configs?
[10:29] Marco Alvarez: We have an IaC module for Dedicated provisioning and a private Helm chart for on-prem bundles. We'll include links in the runbook.
[10:39] [10:41] Priya Singh: I'll also include a sample migration checklist — common gotchas we've seen: implicit role tokens in system messages, hard-coded model names, and differences in streaming chunk sizes. Fixes are usually small.
[10:52] Alex Kim: Perfect. Unless there's anything else, we'll close and follow up with the attachments.
[10:57] Juliette Moreau: Thanks everyone.
[10:58] Chris Moreno: Thanks. Good session.
[11:00] Alex Kim: Thanks all, talk soon."
